JPM.rationale: JPMorgan Chase demonstrates strong fundamental health with accelerating earnings trajectory: Q1 2026 EPS of $5.94 beat estimates by $0.44, representing 17.2% YoY growth and 10% revenue growth. The bank maintains industry-leading profitability with 17.5% ROE and 31.5% net margins, supported by its dominant #1 position in US deposits, global investment banking fees (17 consecutive years), and $7.1T in AUM. The diversified business model across consumer banking, CIB, commercial banking, and AWM provides earnings resilience. However, valuation is mixed: at 13.7x P/E, JPM trades at the low end of its 1-year range (13.7-17.8x), suggesting some discount to recent history, but P/B of 2.2x remains elevated versus the 5-year average of ~1.8x mentioned in news. The recent 3% pullback following CEO Dimon's May 27 comments about higher expenses (~$106B, up $1B from prior guidance) and potential $10-20B acquisition spending creates a modest near-term headwind, though this also represents a potential re-rating catalyst if acquisitions prove accretive. Macro backdrop is supportive with stable rates (Fed Funds at 3.63%) and low VIX (15.7), though rising 10Y yields (4.45%) and oil prices ($92.65) introduce some uncertainty. The stock's -3.1% quarterly decline versus strong fundamentals creates a mild entry opportunity.
